pill.desc: clear, colorless liquid in a single-dose vial

clues.kinetics: Pharmacokinetics in pediatric patients resemble those in adults, with no apparent difference in patients above or below 65 years of age.
clues.substance: A 165-amino acid recombinant molecule made in mammalian cells, with a molecular weight of about 30,400 daltons.
clues.product: Approved under a BLA as single-dose vials of 2,000 to 10,000 units/mL and multiple-dose vials of 20,000 units/2 mL.
clues.safety: Boxed warning for death, heart attack, stroke, clots and tumor progression. Contraindicated in uncontrolled hypertension, pure red cell aplasia and serious allergic reactions.
clues.indication: Anemia from chronic kidney disease in patients on or off dialysis, from zidovudine in HIV, and from chemotherapy; also reducing transfusions in some surgery.
clues.mechanism: Stimulates red cell production by the same mechanism as the body's own erythropoietin.

tell: A recombinant erythropoietin that also carries an indication to reduce red cell transfusions in elective, noncardiac surgery.
